question: A2 transient sample-only learning is due to a SAC semantic/sign/target bug, or to an overly strong entropy target?

semantics.bootstrap_semantics: terminated masks bootstrap; truncation remains bootstrap-compatible
implementation_findings: Twin target critics and the categorical expectation are present.
The actor and alpha loss signs are standard and internally consistent.
No Gumbel/continuous conversion or hidden target-actor substitution was found.
No formula, sign, termination-mask, or target-update defect was found in this bounded audit.

configuration.target_entropy_policy: 0.98*log(9), approximately 98% of the maximum categorical entropy

scale_check.interpretation: The entropy term is not numerically dominant relative to Q, but alpha rises to approximately 0.98 and drives the policy close to uniform entropy. This is a strong exploration target for a 9-action task and is a plausible contributor to the transient sample-only signal; it is not proven causal by this audit.

scientific_result.fixed_seed_reevaluation: argmax strict CE 0/20 at every checkpoint; sample strict CE 6/20 at 25k, 5/20 at 50k, then 0/20 at 75k and 100k
scientific_result.causal_conclusion: No implementation semantic bug identified. Strong near-max target entropy/temperature behavior is the leading bounded semantic hypothesis, but causal isolation would require a new registered experiment and is not authorized in this audit.
scientific_result.next_gate: Keep A2 training and 300k extension locked; retain report for MASTER decision.
